recommendation: Keep this source fix. It resolves obvious current-spec defects that would mislead implementers using the active DosageCondition datatype. Do not treat this as deciding the broader FHIR-51540 R6 dosage redesign or the already-audited FHIR-26899 Extension Pack follow-up; those remain separate work if Pharmacy wants additional semantic changes such as step-level conditions or legacy extension migration.
issue_request: FHIR-15136 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. It asked FHIR-core datatypes to support conditional doses, including examples such as insulin sliding scale, doses based on INR, and doses based on blood pressure. The final resolution was to add an extension and examples.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly names FHIR-15136. Git history shows cb366d831c added source/datatypes/dosage-extensions-spreadsheet.xml in January 2019 with the message "added an extension to Dosage datatype to handle conditional dosing", matching the issue's extension-based resolution. Pharmacy Confluence minutes from late 2019 also tracked FHIR-15136 as Conditional Dosages and called for CDS/oncology/NCPDP examples. Later extension-specific work, including FHIR-26899, was applied separately, and that legacy extension source is no longer active in current core fhir.ini.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini actively lists Dosage, DosageDetails, DosageSafety, and DosageCondition as datatypes and maps them to the dosage page under the Pharmacy work group. The later R6 dosage rework around FHIR-51540 introduced an active DosageCondition datatype and dosage examples, but the new DosageCondition source retained copied RelativeTime wording, wrong/duplicated value set metadata, a stale ConditionDetails path, and an example using the invalid code fragment "if needed" instead of "if-needed". A 2026 Zulip thread about R6 DosageCondition vs. the dosage-conditions extension independently called out the same documentation and binding-label problems while treating broader R6 semantics as still needing use-case-driven review.
reconciliation: Changed active core source in source/datatypes/dosage.xml, source/datatypes/dosagecondition.xml, source/datatypes/codesystem-dosage-condition-code.xml, source/datatypes/valueset-dosage-condition-code.xml, source/datatypes/valueset-dosage-condition-details.xml, and source/dosage-examples.html. The changes describe dosage applicability rather than RelativeTime anchors, correct the DosageCondition code binding and value[x] wording, give dosage-condition-code/details value sets distinct and accurate metadata, fix the CodeSystem property path, and align the example and note with the actual if-needed code.
source_changes: source/datatypes/dosage.xml: fixed Dosage.condition definition typo so the conditional applicability rule is readable.
source/datatypes/dosagecondition.xml: replaced copied RelativeTime/root/code descriptions and corrected value[x] wording for the active DosageCondition datatype.
source/datatypes/codesystem-dosage-condition-code.xml: corrected the type property path to DosageCondition.value[x] and cleaned condition-code definitions.
source/datatypes/valueset-dosage-condition-code.xml: replaced copied Dose Limit Scope/Additional Binding Purpose metadata with DosageCondition code metadata.
source/datatypes/valueset-dosage-condition-details.xml: gave the details value set its own canonical URL and clearer title/description.
source/dosage-examples.html: changed the example code fragment to if-needed and updated the note to refer to DosageCondition.code rather than contextCode.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue adjusted the legacy conditional Dosage extension; it already has an external-repo audit commit on the combined branch and helps explain why this fix targets the active core datatype rather than the retired core extension spreadsheet.
R6 dosage rework created the active DosageCondition datatype and examples where these defects live, but its Jira status is Resolved - change required rather than Published/Applied in this run.
FHIR-15136 comments and Pharmacy minutes cite it as an example source for dosage clarification, but it concerns MedicationRequest.reasonCode and was not needed for this bounded source fix.
Later no-change decision not to make the conditional Dosage extension more prominent supports avoiding extra core links or prominence changes for the legacy extension.
